claim_scope: Pre-registered, GT-free holdout replication of the corridor1-1 10k arm C' method (m9-openloris-sparse-stereo-10000-v1.json's adopted 10k pipeline: A2 base-only frontier -> B rank0-prefix stereo8 bridge over the unregistered tail -> C' stereo8 bridge admitted onto rank 0's own frames, mapped without --rank0-pair-prefix) on an untouched OpenLORIS sequence (corridor1-5) not used to form the arm-C' hypothesis. Candidate generation, matching, and admission are GT-free throughout; ground truth is used only for the post-mapping scores. The pre-registered holdout gates (P1-P4) are evaluated against control B6, per the protocol registered before any mapping was run on this sequence.
background: m9-openloris-sparse-stereo-10000-v1.json found that on corridor1-1's 10k tier, B6's rank-0 component had a badly degenerate Sim(3) scale (0.045) caused by the base snapshot having almost no cross-sensor (stereo) edges, and that admitting the stride-8 stereo8 bridge directly onto rank 0's own frames (arm C', no --rank0-pair-prefix) corrected this to near-metric scale (0.989) and cut aggregate RMSE 14.4x. Because that hypothesis was formed by inspecting a GT-derived Sim(3) scale on corridor1-1, corridor1-1 is a development set with respect to it (caveat (a) of that file). This step re-runs the identical pre-registered method on corridor1-5 -- an OpenLORIS sequence never used in forming or tuning the arm-C' hypothesis -- as the pre-registered holdout check.

holdout_selection.rationale: corridor1-5 was chosen as the holdout sequence because (1) it is an untouched OpenLORIS session with respect to the arm-C' hypothesis -- no prior m8/m9 step staged, mapped, or inspected corridor1-5 -- and (2) among the corridor1-* sequences not yet used for m9 development, it is the largest available (4381 frames/camera, 8762 images), giving the most statistical power to the holdout gates.

deviation_rig_timestamp_tolerance.commit: afd7c91de40796d9be205db12f4b32e01da252bb (feat: expose rig timestamp repair tolerance)
deviation_rig_timestamp_tolerance.commit_message:
Add --timestamp-tolerance-seconds (default 0.001, unchanged) to build_openloris_rig_manifest.py. The corridor1-5 holdout contains one split cam1/cam2 exposure pair 1.03 ms apart, just over the 1 ms default.

Verified GT-free before any mapping: default output is byte-identical to the corridor1-1 5k/10k manifests; at 0.002 only the header changes there (repaired_pairs stays 1); on corridor1-5 the frame rows are identical for 0.002, 0.005 and 0.01, so the holdout result is insensitive to the choice.
deviation_rig_timestamp_tolerance.reason: corridor1-5's rig manifest has one split cam1/cam2 exposure pair (cam2_007012.png / cam1_007013.png, joined as frame_id 3506 in the emitted manifest) whose timestamps are 1.03 ms apart -- just over the 1 ms default --timestamp-tolerance-seconds, which would otherwise fail rig-frame grouping for that pair.

rig_manifest_evidence.verified_by: grep '007012\|007013' across rig-manifest-v1.txt and pipeline artifacts: frame_id 3506 maps to exactly this cam1/cam2 pair

deviation_rig_timestamp_tolerance.inertness_evidence: Per the afd7c91 commit message (verified GT-free before any mapping was run): (1) on corridor1-1, the default (0.001) rig manifest output is byte-identical to the frozen 5k/10k manifests used in prior m9 steps, and raising the tolerance to 0.002 changes only the header line (repaired_pairs stays 1) -- no F row changes; (2) on corridor1-5 itself, the F rows are identical across 0.002, 0.005, and 0.01, so the holdout mapping result is insensitive to the exact tolerance chosen within that range.

analysis.1_no_generalization_claim: The holdout gates fail (P2 and P3 FAIL), so this step makes no generalization or performance claim for arm C' beyond corridor1-1. Arm C' remains, as recorded in m9-openloris-sparse-stereo-10000-v1.json, a corridor1-1 development result: adopted as the current 10k development pipeline there, but not shown here to transfer cleanly to a second, untouched sequence.
analysis.2_corridor1_1_failure_mode_absent_here: The specific failure mode arm C' was designed to fix on corridor1-1 -- a base graph (A2's rank 0) with almost no cross-sensor edges, producing a severely degenerate Sim(3) scale (0.045) -- does not occur on corridor1-5. corridor1-5's base-only A2 already registers 4227/4381 frames (96.5%) with a moderately reasonable rank-0 scale of 0.8958756856155219 (~0.896), far from corridor1-1's 0.045. Corroborating this, 60 of the 200 rank-0-targeted stereo8 candidates in arm C' were already present as verified edges in the base graph before this arm ran (corridor1-1's 10k arm C' found only 13 of 244 already present) -- i.e. corridor1-5's base pair graph already carries substantially more cross-sensor structure around rank 0's frames than corridor1-1's did.
analysis.3_mixed_effect_on_holdout: Arm C's effect on corridor1-5 is mixed rather than uniformly positive. Rank 0's own metrics: p95 improves (1.3757093632446031 -> 1.0985071037189786 m) and sim3_scale moves toward metric (0.8958756856155219 -> 0.9221384796093484), consistent with corridor1-1's direction of effect -- but rank 0's RMSE regresses (0.7511905442437915 -> 0.7814617759409137 m), opposite to corridor1-1 where every rank-0 metric improved together. At the aggregate level, RMSE regresses +2.128% vs control B6 (0.6234934533417992 -> 0.6367624133319092 m) while p95 improves -10.16% (1.1845623943814065 -> 1.0641870737390404 m). Because P2 requires BOTH metrics to improve, the gate fails on the RMSE leg alone.
analysis.4_next_steps: Open follow-on question (GT-free, to be investigated without touching groundtruth.txt): why does corridor1-1's base graph lack same-frame cross-sensor pairs around its rank-0 frontier while corridor1-5's base graph already has them, given both runs use identical temporal-pyramid/rig-local-grouping candidate generation flags (--pair-source temporal-pyramid --rig-local-grouping --retrieval-topk 32 --temporal-pyramid-max-offset 32) and the same 7n candidate budget scaling. No COLMAP control was run on corridor1-5 in this step, and no README/registry promotion is made -- this file records a pre-registered holdout check, not a benchmark result.

decision.outcome: 2 of 4 pre-registered holdout gates PASS (P1, P4); 2 FAIL (P2, P3)
decision.summary: Running the corridor1-1-derived arm C' method unmodified on the untouched corridor1-5 sequence registers 4241/4381 frames (vs B6's 4237/4381, P1 PASS) with all stages staying well under the 2 GiB RSS budget (max 1,223,600 KiB, P4 PASS). However, the aggregate accuracy gate fails: RMSE regresses 2.1% vs control B6 even though p95 improves 10.2% (P2 FAIL, since both legs are required). The per-component scale gate also fails: component-001's Sim(3) scale (0.8712521172280204) sits outside [0.9, 1.1], but this is a pre-existing property of the base graph (already 0.8750503731101259 in A2, untouched by arm C's rank0-targeted bridge) rather than something arm C' introduced or could fix (P3 FAIL). Root-cause analysis shows the corridor1-1 failure mode arm C' was built to correct (a near-edgeless, severely scale-degenerate rank-0 base graph) is largely absent in corridor1-5 -- its A2 rank 0 already registers 96.5% of frames with a scale of 0.896, and 60 of 200 candidate rank0-stereo8 pairs were already present in the base graph.
decision.not_claimed: COLMAP parity, wall-clock/performance superiority, or that arm C' generalizes as a corridor-agnostic accuracy improvement. This holdout run establishes that arm C' does NOT clear its own pre-registered accuracy and per-component-scale gates on a second sequence, so m9-openloris-sparse-stereo-10000-v1.json's corridor1-1 result should continue to be read as a development-set finding, not a validated general method.

caveats.a: P2 fails on the RMSE leg by a small margin (2.1% regression) while p95 improves substantially (10.2%); a practitioner weighting p95 (tail behavior) more heavily than mean RMSE might read this arm more favorably, but the pre-registered gate as written requires both metrics to improve, and this step reports the gate result as pre-registered rather than re-litigating the threshold post hoc.
caveats.b: P3's failing component (component-001, rank 1) was never touched by arm C's stereo8 bridge (which targets only rank 0's own frames) and was already outside the [0.9, 1.1] band in A2 before any stereo8 bridging ran on corridor1-5 at all. This means P3's failure reflects a pre-existing property of corridor1-5's rank-1 component's base graph, not a regression introduced by this step's method -- but the gate, as pre-registered, does not distinguish pre-existing from introduced scale problems, so it is reported as FAIL per its literal text.
caveats.c: No COLMAP control was run on corridor1-5 in this step (context_not_gated numbers from other benchmark files, such as the corridor1-1 COLMAP 10k control, are not directly comparable to corridor1-5 and are omitted here rather than juxtaposed misleadingly).
caveats.d: This file's own archive_sha256 provenance has an internal discrepancy between the final source-audit.json (archive_sha256=null, documented as not computed) and an in-flight copy embedded in logs/stage.log (a populated archive_sha256 for the full tar). See holdout_selection.unverifiable_note above; this was not independently reconciled.
